ratings.is_biologically_coherent_comments: It is logically sound but my one reservation is that the presented RCT is about BP control in type 2 diabetics. While the explanation about age subgroup analysis makes sense, it has to be pertinent to the specific patient population being addressed. (in this case type 2 diabetes but SPRINT subgroup analysis finding was about non-diabetics).
ratings.is_causally_plausible_comments: Older age adults may have other competing risks that may make it more difficult to uncover potential benefits of intense BP management. On the other hand, there is heterogeneous nature of the older age adults, such as frailty factors etc.
ratings.is_literature_backed_comments: "In the Trial of Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Older Patients with Hypertension", intense BP control resulted in reduced CV events, supporting the existence of differential effects (i.e., in older patients, intense BP has CV benefits).
ratings.comments: frailty factor has not been adequately accounted for in other studies.

ratings.is_literature_backed_comments: There aren't much studies and evidence around this as far as I am aware of.

ratings.is_clinically_actionable_comments: Higher BP patients can be a better target of intensive BP therapy -- however, that is somewhat intuitive.

ratings.is_biologically_coherent_comments: The explanation states that patients with blunt trauma benefit more from TXA than those with penetrating trauma. This paper showed no significant differences between these groups and, if anything, suggested a greater benefit with penetrating trauma.
ratings.is_causally_plausible_comments: The statement is biologically plausible and probably accurate. However, to my knowledge, it has not been definitively shown that hyperfibrinolysis is more responsive to antifibrinolytic therapy. This point is still debated.
ratings.is_clinically_actionable_comments: If the statement is accepted as true, it would support having a lower threshold for giving TXA in blunt trauma patients.
ratings.is_literature_backed_comments: While the explanation is biologically plausible, there is no clinical evidence to support it.

ratings.is_causally_plausible_comments: The explanation states that the most hypotensive patients benefit more from TXA. This is suggested from the data, but the subgroup analysis showed no significant differences between these groups.
This study did not include a subgroup analysis specifically looking at isolated TBI vs combined TBI + body trauma. CRASH-3 was probably underpowered, so hard to make definitive conclusions.
The explanation states there is a difference between subgroups. There was a suggestion of a difference, but no significant difference found in this study.
